usageNotes: Use this to register a new authentication realm (AD, LDAP, OpenID Connect, PAM, or local PVE) so users can log in via that backend. Requires the `Realm.Allocate` privilege on `/access/realm`. The required parameters differ by `type`: AD/LDAP need `server1`, `base_dn`, and `user_attr`; OpenID needs `issuer-url`, `client-id`, and `client-key`; PAM and PVE need only `realm` and `type`.

examples.summary: Add an LDAP realm backed by an internal directory server

tips: Set `check-connection: true` to validate bind credentials and server reachability at creation time rather than discovering failures on first login.
Use `mode: ldap+starttls` or `mode: ldaps` instead of the deprecated `secure` boolean; enforce `sslversion: tlsv1_2` or higher.
For OpenID realms, `username-claim` defaults to `sub` (an opaque identifier); set it to `email` or `preferred_username` for human-readable PVE usernames.
The `autocreate` flag creates PVE user records on first successful login but does not assign permissions — assign roles separately after users appear.
To make this realm the default shown on the login screen, set `default: true`; only one realm can hold this flag at a time.
The LDAP bind password is stored in `/etc/pve/priv/realm/<REALM>.pw` on the PVE host — treat that file as a secret.
